scope_note: These tiers describe fixture realism and integration depth only. They are not production-effectiveness claims and do not replace an uncontaminated independent Arena assessment.

limitations: Static source-fragment reasoning only; no runtime target is executed.
Does not measure independent verification, remediation, regression generation, or release gating.

benchmarks.reset_strategy: Each bounded proof owns a deterministic LOCAL fixture reset or fresh fixture instance.
limitations: Measures proof primitives rather than the full SecHelix agent workflow.
Loopback synthetic fixtures do not establish production behavior.

benchmarks.reset_strategy: Each benchmark run starts a fresh literal-loopback fixture and fresh browser context.
limitations: Browser availability may block measurement and must not be converted into a clean result.

benchmarks.reset_strategy: Valid and invalid sessions use isolated contexts; revocation fixtures use deterministic LOCAL reset state.
limitations: Measures browser session isolation and revocation integration, not end-to-end application behavior.
Session credential values are execution-only and are not persisted.

benchmarks.reset_strategy: The SQLite workflow store is dropped and recreated from a deterministic seed before each self-test run, restoring the order and removing refund state.
limitations: The self-test measures the fixture contract only; it does not score SecHelix discovery, independent verification, remediation, regression generation, or release-gate correctness.
This is a controlled literal-loopback single-service fixture and does not establish production effectiveness.

benchmarks.reset_strategy: The shared SQLite state is dropped and recreated from a deterministic seed, clearing workflow, outbox, and ledger state before each self-test.
limitations: The self-test measures the controlled two-service fixture contract only; it does not score SecHelix discovery, verification, remediation, regression generation, or release-gate correctness.
The asynchronous boundary is a deterministic SQLite outbox between literal-loopback services, not a production message broker or production-effectiveness measurement.
